items.title: Is it smart to read on your phone? The impact of reading format and culture on the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants read pairs of short newspaper-style articles... and were later assessed on their memory for critical and general details, as well as inferential judgements related to the retracted information.
judge.evidence_topic: Participants read pairs of short newspaper-style articles containing a critical piece of information that was either retracted or not retracted... Chinese readers... were more affected by the continued influence of the misinformation.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga diretamente o efeito de influência continuada da informação falsa usando materiais com retratação, é um experimento empírico, o método descrito bae com o resumo e o achado extraído é fiel aos resultados apresentados.

items.title: Mechanisms in continued influence: The impact of misinformation corrections on source perceptions

judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that an external correction (i.e., a new source labeling misinformation as false) influences perceptions of the misinformation source, and these perceptions of the misinformation source then correlated with belief in the misinformation. Study 2 replicated the results of Study 1 and used source derogation to manipulate misinformation source perceptions and further lessen continued belief. Study 3 was a preregistered replication of previous results using new methodology.
judge.evidence_topic: Research on the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has demonstrated that misinformation continues to influence people's beliefs and judgments even after it has been corrected.
judge.reason: O artigo trata explicitamente do efeito de influência continuada da informação falsa, com três estudos experimentais que medem crença após ume correção. Não ha indícios de conteúdos político, de vacinas ou COVID-19. Os dados extraídos (metodo e achado) batem com o resumo.

items.title: Vaccination against misinformation: The inoculation technique reduces the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: The results show that the reliability of corrections’ sources did not affect their processing when participants were not inoculated. However, inoculated participants relied on misinformation less when the correction came from a highly credible source.
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect of misinformation (CIE) is a phenomenon in which certain information, although retracted and corrected, still has an impact on event reporting, reasoning, inference, and decisions.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e relata experimento com participantes humanos medindo crença/raciocínio após correção, usando materiais neutros (sem conotação política ou de saúde). Os dados extraídos condizem com o resumo e o achado principal é diretamente suportado.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The term “continued influence effect” (CIE) refers to the phenomenon that discredited and obsolete information continues to affect behavior and beliefs.
judge.reason: O artigo trata explicitamente do efeito de influência continuada da desinformação (CIE), com experimentos usando materiais neutros (fake news em geral, sem conotação polótica ou de saúdo). items.title: Cause typicality and the continued influence effect
